summary: Tested the CPF-login / admin / RapidoCar+MooveCar refactor. Backend: 20/20 pytest pass (new file test_cpf_admin_apps.py). Covered: CPF validation (422), new CPF -> pending, pending/blocked get no token, approved login returns a token and a masked CPF, CPF IP limit (20 -> 429, which also blocks the approved CPF), admin login 401 and 5-fail 429, admin list filters with counts, PATCH approve/block/name, DELETE then 404, driver token rejected on admin routes and admin token rejected on driver routes, blocking a driver makes their existing token 401, per-app settings PUT (moove-only change leaves rapido unchanged), validation 422s, rides bulk and filters by app/status, removed endpoints 404/405. Frontend (375x667): login mask, invalid CPF error, pending notice, admin login and wrong-password error, admin pending list, approve, block, delete with confirm, approved login to Painel, only 3 tabs, no earnings/99/simulator, independent LIGADO/DESLIGADO toggles, filters-summary-moove opens Filtros with MooveCar selected, each app keeps its own filters (moove 13,50 / rapido 8), schedule/alert switches, Aprender with RapidoCar/MooveCar segments and only a 'Botão Aceitar' target, Histórico app and status chips, Conta account-cpf, a blocked driver is signed out to /login on their next request. Found and fixed a CRITICAL routing bug: logged-out users (on first open and after Sair) were sent to /admin instead of /login. Found a HIGH security issue: the rate limits can be bypassed by sending a fake X-Forwarded-For header. Deprecated packages: none found (no expo-av, expo-barcode-scanner or expo-background-fetch). SafeAreaView issues: none found.

critical.issue: client_ip() takes the FIRST X-Forwarded-For entry, and the client controls that entry. Sending a random 'X-Forwarded-For: 10.x.x.x' gives a fresh rate-limit bucket every time. Verified: each fake IP got its own 5-fail admin counter and its own 20-attempt CPF counter. So the admin password can be brute-forced without limit, and pending CPFs can be spammed without limit. Fix: key on the IP the ingress adds (the right-most X-Forwarded-For entry, or X-Real-IP if the ingress sets it), not the left-most one.

minor.issue: Each pending/blocked check calls record_fail on the IP key, and check_limit runs before the CPF is looked up. A pending driver who taps 'Entrar' 20 times in 15 minutes locks out every driver on the same IP, including APPROVED ones (verified: the approved CPF gets 429). On mobile-carrier CGNAT many drivers share one IP. Suggest: do not count pending re-checks of an already-registered CPF, or key the limit per IP+CPF for existing CPFs and always let approved CPFs log in.

CPF works as the only credential. Anyone who knows an approved driver's CPF (not a secret in Brazil) gets a 30-day token. This is by design per the user's request, but the user should be told about this risk.

ui_bugs.issue: FIXED BY TESTER. When the guard is false, expo-router falls back to the alphabetically first route, which is 'admin'. So a fresh logged-out open of '/' and logout from Conta both landed on the Administrador screen instead of Login. Fix applied: redirectTo="/login" on the signed-in group and redirectTo="/" on the login group (supported in expo-router 58). Verified: fresh load -> /login, logout -> /login, visiting /login while logged in -> Painel, admin still reachable from Login.

Seen once: the first tap on auto-accept-toggle-moove right after Painel appeared (still in the login->Painel transition) sent no PUT and the state stayed DESLIGADO. With a 2.5s wait it always worked. Low-priority flake, probably the stack transition swallowing the tap.

issues: The app chips and status chips share one horizontal scroll row. At 375px, 'RapidoCar' gets cut at the left and 'Recusadas' is off-screen when a later chip is selected. Consider two rows (app row + status row).
The filter chip row overflows at 375px (the 'Bloqueados (n)' label is cut off). It is acceptable because the row scrolls, but there is no scroll hint.

action_items: HIGH: Fix the rate-limit bypass in server.py client_ip(): stop trusting the left-most X-Forwarded-For value. Use the ingress-appended right-most entry (or X-Real-IP set by the ingress).
Stop counting pending re-checks of an existing CPF as IP failures, or exempt approved CPFs from the IP 429, so one pending driver cannot lock out approved drivers on a shared carrier IP.
Keep the redirectTo fix in app/_layout.tsx (tester change) and verify on the Android APK that the logged-out first open shows Login, not Admin.
Optional: split the Histórico chips into app and status rows.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py client_ip(): fwd.split(',')[0] is spoofable by the client. This is the root cause of the rate-limit bypass.
server.py login_cpf(): check_limit runs before the CPF lookup, so the approved-driver path is blocked by other users' pending attempts.
The admin token is kept only in component state (admin.tsx) and is never persisted. Good.
The legacy settings migration in get_settings() maps old auto_accept to apps.rapido.enabled. Looks right.
updated_files: /app/frontend/app/_layout.tsx (added redirectTo="/login" and redirectTo="/" to the two Stack.Protected groups)

success_rate.backend: 100% (20/20); 1 HIGH security issue found by code review and confirmed by test
success_rate.frontend: ~95% (all requested flows pass after the routing fix)

seed_data_creation: None kept. Throwaway CPFs were created and deleted through the admin API/UI by id (pytest fixtures, 608.477.737-60 deleted via the UI, one more deleted via the API). Its settings: both apps enabled=false, schedule off, alert on; moove.min_fare=12 was already set before my test ran and was restored to that value.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run with: cd /app && python -m pytest backend/tests/test_cpf_admin_apps.py -n 0. The tests use random X-Forwarded-For IPs for the rate-limit tests, which only works because of the spoofing bug; once client_ip is fixed, those 2 tests (test_cpf_rate_limit_429, test_admin_rate_limit_429) must be rewritten or run last, because they would lock out the test IP. The test file reads EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL from frontend/.env and ADMIN_PASSWORD from backend/.env. For urllib calls to the public URL, send a User-Agent header (Cloudflare returns 1010/403 without one). Rides tests use a temporary approved user so the real driver's history is untouched.
rca_of_issue: Admin-instead-of-login: expo-router Stack.Protected redirects to the navigator anchor, which here is the alphabetically first available route ('admin'). Repro: clear storage, open '/', and you land on /admin; or log in, then Conta > Sair, and you land on /admin. Fix: redirectTo on Stack.Protected (SDK 58). Verified in the web preview.
